findings.text: s18 offers `ledger.load(..., picker_only=True)` as a mechanism that makes the refresh "decode no full run payload" while the published profile "includes the promoted row", but no such path exists: the promotion has just moved the ledger, so `_indexed_data` re-reads its source, and the aggregate fallback at reckon/ledger.py:2102 parses every row BEFORE projecting (`data["runs"] = [picker_record(row) ...]` at :2106-2110), while the refused-refresh snapshot at :1662 is served only when `_open_current_index` (:1087) sees an unmoved aggregate — which is precisely the case in which the appended row is absent from it. A node taking the first branch fails the decode assertion; a node taking it and then adding a fold has taken the second branch

findings.reason: a worker implementing the memo exactly as written ships a config-blind cache that no fixture in the section's own four cases can detect, because every case uses one config.
findings.text: s17 keys the new in-process memo on "the ledger's own change stamp" alone, but every reading `_readings` builds carries `surface_opt_in=_surface_opt_in(backend_name, config)` (reckon/budget.py:658, :513-525), a config fact, and `latest_recorded` is called with `config=` from four caller sites (pace_report.py:1617, crew/dispatch_admission.py:388, crew/resumption.py:926, crew/routing.py:481); the first caller's config therefore freezes every later caller's opt-in until the ledger moves
